column1: Where does control go when a catchable error occurs inside TRY?
column2:
To the associated CATCH block.
The remaining statements in that TRY block are skipped.
Review source

column1: Where does control go after TRY finishes without an error?
column2:
To the statement after END CATCH.
The associated CATCH block is skipped.
Review source

column1: Where does execution normally resume when CATCH finishes without rethrowing or returning?
column2:
After END CATCH.
It does not resume at the failed statement inside TRY.
Review source

column1: Why rethrow an unexpected caught error after cleanup?
column2:
The caller does not receive the caught exception automatically.
A CATCH block that only logs an error can hide the failure from its caller.
Review source

column1: Which compilation errors bypass TRY...CATCH at the same execution level?
column2:
Errors such as syntax errors that prevent the batch from running.
The same-level handler cannot run when its batch cannot compile.
Review source

column1: How can an outer TRY catch a missing-table error from dynamic SQL?
column2:
Execute that statement through sp_executesql inside TRY.
Object resolution then occurs at a lower execution level.
Review source

column1: What happens to local CATCH handling if an error closes the database connection?
column2:
It cannot run in that terminated connection.
Some severity-20-or-higher errors remain catchable if the connection survives.
Review source

column1: How does TRY...CATCH treat a severity-10 informational message?
column2:
It does not transfer control to CATCH.
Messages with severity 10 or lower are outside its catchable error range.
Review source

column1: Why does ERROR_MESSAGE remain reliable after other successful statements in the same CATCH?
column2:
Its value is scoped to the caught error.
Successful statements and repeated reads do not consume that error information.
Review source

column1: What does ERROR_PROCEDURE return for a caught error raised outside any stored procedure or trigger?
column2:
NULL.
An ad hoc batch error can still have an error number and message.
Review source

column1: In a nested CATCH, which error does ERROR_MESSAGE describe?
column2:
The error that invoked that CATCH.
The outer CATCH keeps its own error context.
Review source

column1: What happens to the original error number when CATCH uses bare THROW;?
column2:
It is preserved.
Creating a new numbered exception replaces that number.
Review source

column1: Why must logging precede bare THROW in a CATCH?
column2:
THROW transfers control, so later logging statements do not run.
Log the details before propagating the failure to the caller.
Review source

column1: What can THROW's state distinguish when the same error number is raised at several locations?
column2:
The location that raised the error.
Assign distinct states to different raise sites.
Review source

column1: Which function can prepare a formatted message for THROW?
column2:
FORMATMESSAGE.
Assign its result to a message variable before passing that variable to THROW.
Review source

column1: Why must code using RAISERROR handle transaction rollback explicitly?
column2:
RAISERROR does not honor SET XACT_ABORT.
An error message alone is not transaction cleanup.
Review source

column1: What groups several data changes into an all-or-nothing operation?
column2:
An explicit transaction with appropriate commit and rollback handling.
TRY...CATCH alone does not make several statements atomic.
Review source

column1: For a procedure-owned all-or-nothing transaction, when does the success path commit?
column2:
After all required operations succeed.
Keep the commit on the successful TRY path.
Review source

column1: Why does @@TRANCOUNT > 0 not prove that COMMIT is allowed?
column2:
It reports transaction count, not committability.
Use XACT_STATE() to check whether the transaction can be committed.
Review source

column1: Why must CATCH still check transaction state with XACT_ABORT ON?
column2:
A caught error can leave an active transaction that cannot be committed.
Automatic abort does not guarantee rollback before CATCH executes.
Review source

column1: Which error phase is not covered by XACT_ABORT?
column2:
Compilation, including syntax errors.
XACT_ABORT is a run-time error option.
Review source

column1: With XACT_ABORT OFF, what can happen after a statement-level runtime error?
column2:
Only the failed statement rolls back, leaving the transaction active.
Other errors can still abort the entire transaction.
Review source

column1: Why check for an active transaction before ROLLBACK in CATCH?
column2:
Some errors already roll back the transaction.
Rolling back with no active transaction causes another error.
Review source

column1: What rollback is permitted when XACT_STATE() = -1?
column2:
A full transaction rollback, not a savepoint rollback.
The transaction cannot perform writes or commit.
Review source

column1: For a procedure-owned uncommittable transaction, when can CATCH insert into a normal ErrorLog table?
column2:
After fully rolling back the failed transaction.
An uncommittable transaction rejects ordinary table writes, including logging.
Review source

column1: When only the outer procedure starts a shared transaction, which procedure coordinates rollback in the unit's pattern?
column2:
The outer procedure.
The inner procedure rethrows so the owning outer CATCH can clean up.
Review source

column1: If @@TRANCOUNT is 2, what does ROLLBACK TRANSACTION without a savepoint do?
column2:
Rolls back the full transaction and sets @@TRANCOUNT to 0.
Nested BEGIN TRANSACTION calls do not create independently rolled-back transactions.
Review source

column1: How can CATCH handle catchable errors from its own logging code?
column2:
Use a nested TRY...CATCH around the logging operation.
An error does not re-enter the CATCH block already running.
Review source

column1: Why is XACT_STATE() = 1 insufficient reason to commit an all-or-nothing operation after an error?
column2:
Committable does not mean every required operation succeeded.
Roll back incomplete work even when the transaction can still be committed.
Review source
